body.text: This is your question for today. Keep it in mind during the games.
Three games tonight: standing, guarded, pinned. Win one and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run the same one again.
Upper vs Lower Body Division Game
Skill Learning Objective (SLO): Entering, for both players.
Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range. One is the upper body player, one is the lower body player. Open hands only.

Upper body player: stay between, outside, or under your partner's arms. Get an underhook, or make his hands touch the mat. You may not touch his legs. Lower body player: touch only the head, hands, and elbows to move them, then touch anywhere behind the leg. You may not go under the arms. Whoever gets there first wins, then you switch roles.

items: The upper body player wins with an underhook, or the other player's hands on the mat.
The lower body player wins with a touch behind the leg, or the other player's hands on the mat.

body.text: SLO: Arriving for the top player, Leaving for the bottom player.
The top player stands. The bottom player sits on the mat with an inside hook and a knee-pit grip.

Bottom player: move from seated to belly up, using your connections to put the top player down on his hips or hands, then wrestle up or stand and make his back touch the mat. Top player: put the bottom player on his back and keep shin contact.

items: The bottom player wins by standing up and reaching the hips, or by making the top player's back touch the mat.
The top player wins with shin contact on the knees or body.

body.text: Back Take, Maintain Chest to Back Contact
SLO: Controlling for the top player, Leaving for the bottom player.
The attacker is in full back control, chest on the defender's back, arms around the shoulders, hooks in. The defender may move freely.

Attacker: keep chest-to-back contact by following the defender wherever he goes. If your hands separate, reconnect them. If a hook comes out, put it back in. Defender: fight the connections to put your back on the mat or turn to face the attacker.

items: The attacker has no time limit. He holds as long as he keeps contact.
The defender wins by getting his back to the mat or turning face to face.

slides.title: How you win it
slides.question: In Back Take, Maintain Chest to Back Contact, what wins it for the top player?

options.text: The attacker has no time limit. He holds as long as he keeps contact.
options.feedback: That is the win condition, and nothing else scores.

options.text: Holding the finish after your partner taps
options.feedback: Never. You let go the second your partner taps. Every single time. The tap is law.

options.text: Hurting your partner because you can
options.feedback: That is the one thing the Back Pin teaches you never to do. Total control, plus the choice not to hurt someone, is the heart of the whole program.

slides.correctText: That is how you win today.
